Bottom-left (south-west) corner of the area to scan, as `latitude,longitude`. The total box area is capped per `zoom` level (see the `zoom` parameter).

  **Example:** `40.63,-74.10`

parameters.name: top_right
parameters.description:

  **Example:** `40.81,-73.87`

parameters.name: zoom
parameters.description:
Google Maps zoom level for the scan - the same zoom value Google Maps uses (higher is more zoomed in, returning finer detail over a smaller maximum area). Each zoom level has a maximum bounding-box area; to cover a larger area, use a lower zoom level.

  **Allowed values:** `11-16`

  **Maximum area per zoom:**

  - zoom 11: 8000 km²
  - zoom 12: 2000 km²
  - zoom 13: 500 km² (default)
  - zoom 14: 125 km²
  - zoom 15: 30 km²
  - zoom 16: 8 km²

  **Default:** `13`

get.description:
Returns live traffic incidents (accidents, construction zones, road closures, and other slowdowns) within the bounding box defined by two corner coordinates. Each alert includes its incident type and precise latitude/longitude.

The bounding box area is capped per `zoom` level (higher zoom returns finer detail over a smaller maximum area). To scan a larger area, use a lower zoom level.

parameters.description:

`Illinois,Florida,Ontario`

parameters.description:

**Examples:**

parameters.name: district
parameters.description:

Accepts up to 32 values by repeating the parameter *(e.g. `district=value1&district=value2`)*.

`Coffee shop,Hotel,Bakery`

parameters.name: business_category_id

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `business_category_id=bakery&business_category_id=catholic_church&business_category_id=psychotherapist`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses by Google's internal entity-type IDs. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

These are entity types rather than the listing's categories: the values are broad and a listing usually carries several of them, so this is a wide filter.

The IDs are gcids (Google Maps category IDs). For a list of gcids see *https://www.openwebninja.com/blog/all-google-maps-categories*.

**Examples:**

`bakery`

`bakery,catholic_church,psychotherapist`

parameters.name: main_business_category_id

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `main_business_category_id=restaurant&main_business_category_id=hotel&main_business_category_id=dentist`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses by Google's internal ID of the primary category. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

This is the machine ID, not the display label the main_business_category parameter matches, and the two can name different primaries.

The IDs are gcids (Google Maps category IDs). For a list of gcids see *https://www.openwebninja.com/blog/all-google-maps-categories*.

**Examples:**

`restaurant`

`restaurant,hotel,dentist`

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Find businesses by their display name.

`Office of City Treasurer`

`Avante Catering`

`Truist`

parameters.description:
Find businesses by the name on the owner profile.

Accepts up to 32 values by repeating the parameter *(e.g. `owner_name=value1&owner_name=value2`)*.

Values cannot be comma separated here, as a comma can be part of the value. In the POST form, send an array instead.

**Examples:**

`Office of City Treasurer`

parameters.name: phone_number

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `phone_number=+13127443356&phone_number=+12063248900`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses by phone number. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

Send the number with its country code, either in E.164 *(`+14325551234`, URL-encoded as `%2B14325551234`)* or in a decorated form such as `1-432-555-1234`, `(432) 555-1234` or `0014325551234`.

**Examples:**

`+13127443356`

`+13127443356,+12063248900,+13053784725`

Both corners are required, and any field parameter of the Search endpoint can be combined with them.

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description:
Latitude of the center coordinate point of the area to search in.

Required together with lng and radius.

parameters.name: lng
parameters.description:
Longitude of the center coordinate point of the area to search in.

Required together with lat and radius.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description:
Radius of the area to search in, in meters.

**Allowed values:** `1-100000`

parameters.name: business_category

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `business_category=restaurant&business_category=bank&business_category=photography studio`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses carrying a specific category. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

**Examples:**

`restaurant`

`restaurant,bank,photography studio`

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Maximum number of businesses to return.

**Allowed values:** `1-500`

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Pagination cursor for fetching the next page. Pass the `cursor` value returned in the previous response. Omit it on the first request.

**Note:** a cursor is only valid for the exact query that produced it, and it expires. Do not build or edit one.

parameters.name: country

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `country=US&country=MX&country=CA`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses in a specific country, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

For a list of supported country codes see *https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2*.

**Examples:**

`US`

`US,MX,CA`

parameters.name: state

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `state=Illinois&state=Florida&state=Ontario`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses in a specific state or province. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

US states match either way they are sent, by full name or by two-letter code.

**Examples:**

`Illinois`

`Illinois,Florida,Ontario`

`IL,FL`

parameters.name: city
parameters.description:
Find businesses in a specific city.

Accepts up to 32 values by repeating the parameter *(e.g. `city=value1&city=value2`)*.

Values cannot be comma separated here, as a comma can be part of the value. In the POST form, send an array instead.

**Examples:**

`Chicago`

parameters.name: zipcode

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `zipcode=60602&zipcode=98112&zipcode=33186`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses in a specific ZIP / postal code. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

**Examples:**

`60602`

`60602,98112,33186`

parameters.name: district
parameters.description:
Find businesses in a specific district or neighbourhood, when the listing carries one.

Accepts up to 32 values by repeating the parameter *(e.g. `district=value1&district=value2`)*.

Values cannot be comma separated here, as a comma can be part of the value. In the POST form, send an array instead.

**Examples:**

`Chicago Loop`

parameters.name: main_business_category

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `main_business_category=Coffee shop&main_business_category=Hotel&main_business_category=Bakery`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses whose primary category matches. Same value space as the business_category parameter. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

**Examples:**

`Coffee shop`

`Coffee shop,Hotel,Bakery`

parameters.name: business_category_id

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `business_category_id=bakery&business_category_id=catholic_church&business_category_id=psychotherapist`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses by Google's internal entity-type IDs. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

These are entity types rather than the listing's categories: the values are broad and a listing usually carries several of them, so this is a wide filter.

The IDs are gcids (Google Maps category IDs). For a list of gcids see *https://www.openwebninja.com/blog/all-google-maps-categories*.

**Examples:**

`bakery`

`bakery,catholic_church,psychotherapist`

parameters.name: main_business_category_id

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `main_business_category_id=restaurant&main_business_category_id=hotel&main_business_category_id=dentist`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses by Google's internal ID of the primary category. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

This is the machine ID, not the display label the main_business_category parameter matches, and the two can name different primaries.

The IDs are gcids (Google Maps category IDs). For a list of gcids see *https://www.openwebninja.com/blog/all-google-maps-categories*.

**Examples:**

`restaurant`

`restaurant,hotel,dentist`

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Find businesses by their display name.

**Examples:**

`Office of City Treasurer`

`Avante Catering`

`Truist`

parameters.name: owner_name
parameters.description:
Find businesses by the name on the owner profile.

Accepts up to 32 values by repeating the parameter *(e.g. `owner_name=value1&owner_name=value2`)*.

Values cannot be comma separated here, as a comma can be part of the value. In the POST form, send an array instead.

**Examples:**

`Office of City Treasurer`

parameters.name: phone_number

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `phone_number=+13127443356&phone_number=+12063248900`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses by phone number. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

Send the number with its country code, either in E.164 *(`+14325551234`, URL-encoded as `%2B14325551234`)* or in a decorated form such as `1-432-555-1234`, `(432) 555-1234` or `0014325551234`.

**Examples:**

`+13127443356`

`+13127443356,+12063248900,+13053784725`

chicago.value: Office of City Treasurer, 121 N LaSalle St #106, Chicago, IL 60602

seattle.value: Avante Catering, 5600 Delridge Wy SW, Seattle, WA 98106

parameters.description:
Find businesses by their full formatted address, including the business name.

**Examples:**

`Office of City Treasurer, 121 N LaSalle St #106, Chicago, IL 60602`

parameters.name: street_address
parameters.description:
Find businesses by the street line of their address on its own.

A single value is matched loosely, which also finds spelling and abbreviation variants. Several values are matched exactly instead, which narrows the result.

Accepts up to 32 values by repeating the parameter *(e.g. `street_address=value1&street_address=value2`)*.

Values cannot be comma separated here, as a comma can be part of the value. In the POST form, send an array instead.

**Examples:**

`121 N LaSalle St #106`

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `business_id=id1&business_id=id2&business_id=id3`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses by their unique Business Id, matched exactly. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

get.description:
Search business listings within a given distance of a center coordinate point.

`lat`, `lng` and `radius` are all required, and any field parameter of the Search endpoint can be combined with them.

get.description:

Photos are read from Google Maps at request time, so they are live rather than served from the database.

**Note:** `match_count` is the number of photos on this page, not the business's total photo count.

**Note:** `limit` is a maximum and not a promise - a business with fewer photos returns fewer. You have reached the end when a page comes back empty or without a `cursor`.

parameters.name: business_category

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `business_category=restaurant&business_category=bank&business_category=photography studio`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses carrying a specific category. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

**Examples:**

`restaurant`

`restaurant,bank,photography studio`

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Maximum number of businesses to return.

**Allowed values:** `1-500`

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Pagination cursor for fetching the next page. Pass the `cursor` value returned in the previous response. Omit it on the first request.

**Note:** a cursor is only valid for the exact query that produced it, and it expires. Do not build or edit one.

parameters.name: country

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `country=US&country=MX&country=CA`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses in a specific country, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

For a list of supported country codes see *https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2*.

**Examples:**

`US`

`US,MX,CA`

parameters.name: state

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `state=Illinois&state=Florida&state=Ontario`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses in a specific state or province. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

US states match either way they are sent, by full name or by two-letter code.

**Examples:**

`Illinois`

`Illinois,Florida,Ontario`

`IL,FL`

parameters.name: city
parameters.description:
Find businesses in a specific city.

Accepts up to 32 values by repeating the parameter *(e.g. `city=value1&city=value2`)*.

Values cannot be comma separated here, as a comma can be part of the value. In the POST form, send an array instead.

**Examples:**

`Chicago`

parameters.name: zipcode

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `zipcode=60602&zipcode=98112&zipcode=33186`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses in a specific ZIP / postal code. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

**Examples:**

`60602`

`60602,98112,33186`

parameters.name: district
parameters.description:
Find businesses in a specific district or neighbourhood, when the listing carries one.

Accepts up to 32 values by repeating the parameter *(e.g. `district=value1&district=value2`)*.

Values cannot be comma separated here, as a comma can be part of the value. In the POST form, send an array instead.

**Examples:**

`Chicago Loop`

parameters.name: main_business_category

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `main_business_category=Coffee shop&main_business_category=Hotel&main_business_category=Bakery`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses whose primary category matches. Same value space as the business_category parameter. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

**Examples:**

`Coffee shop`

`Coffee shop,Hotel,Bakery`

parameters.name: business_category_id

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `business_category_id=bakery&business_category_id=catholic_church&business_category_id=psychotherapist`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses by Google's internal entity-type IDs. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

These are entity types rather than the listing's categories: the values are broad and a listing usually carries several of them, so this is a wide filter.

The IDs are gcids (Google Maps category IDs). For a list of gcids see *https://www.openwebninja.com/blog/all-google-maps-categories*.

**Examples:**

`bakery`

`bakery,catholic_church,psychotherapist`

parameters.name: main_business_category_id

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `main_business_category_id=restaurant&main_business_category_id=hotel&main_business_category_id=dentist`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses by Google's internal ID of the primary category. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

This is the machine ID, not the display label the main_business_category parameter matches, and the two can name different primaries.

The IDs are gcids (Google Maps category IDs). For a list of gcids see *https://www.openwebninja.com/blog/all-google-maps-categories*.

**Examples:**

`restaurant`

`restaurant,hotel,dentist`

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Find businesses by their display name.

**Examples:**

`Office of City Treasurer`

`Avante Catering`

`Truist`

parameters.name: owner_name
parameters.description:
Find businesses by the name on the owner profile.

Accepts up to 32 values by repeating the parameter *(e.g. `owner_name=value1&owner_name=value2`)*.

Values cannot be comma separated here, as a comma can be part of the value. In the POST form, send an array instead.

**Examples:**

`Office of City Treasurer`

parameters.name: phone_number

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `phone_number=+13127443356&phone_number=+12063248900`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses by phone number. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

Send the number with its country code, either in E.164 *(`+14325551234`, URL-encoded as `%2B14325551234`)* or in a decorated form such as `1-432-555-1234`, `(432) 555-1234` or `0014325551234`.

**Examples:**

`+13127443356`

`+13127443356,+12063248900,+13053784725`

chicago.value: Office of City Treasurer, 121 N LaSalle St #106, Chicago, IL 60602

seattle.value: Avante Catering, 5600 Delridge Wy SW, Seattle, WA 98106

parameters.description:
Find businesses by their full formatted address, including the business name.

**Examples:**

`Office of City Treasurer, 121 N LaSalle St #106, Chicago, IL 60602`

`Avante Catering, 5600 Delridge Wy SW, Seattle, WA 98106`

`Truist, 12390 SW 120th St, Miami, FL 33186`

parameters.name: street_address
parameters.description:
Find businesses by the street line of their address on its own.

A single value is matched loosely, which also finds spelling and abbreviation variants. Several values are matched exactly instead, which narrows the result.

Accepts up to 32 values by repeating the parameter *(e.g. `street_address=value1&street_address=value2`)*.

Values cannot be comma separated here, as a comma can be part of the value. In the POST form, send an array instead.

**Examples:**

`121 N LaSalle St #106`

parameters.name: business_id

multiple.description: The same values as repeated occurrences: `business_id=id1&business_id=id2&business_id=id3`.

parameters.description:
Find businesses by their unique Business Id, matched exactly. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

**Examples:**

`0x102b644d009e013:0xea49e9ee285fa7bf`

`0x102b644d009e013:0xea49e9ee285fa7bf,0x1792d85c519234b:0x91eebb9c864b198d`

post.description:
Search business listings by any combination of the fields below, sent as a JSON body. Same results as the GET form, and the form to use when the query is too long for a URL - for example a list of up to 32 values on several fields at once.

At least one of the filter parameters below is required for search. This form also accepts an area: either `bottom_left` with `top_right`, or `lat` with `lng` and `radius`.

**Note:** `match_count` is the total number of matching businesses, not the number returned on this page. A `cursor` is returned while further pages are available and omitted on the last page.

**Note:** a query that matches nothing is not an error. The response is a `200` with an empty `businesses` array.

lat.description:
Latitude of the center coordinate point of the area to search in.

Send either bottom_left with top_right, or lat with lng and radius - not both, and not a partial group.

lng.description:
Longitude of the center coordinate point of the area to search in.

Send either bottom_left with top_right, or lat with lng and radius - not both, and not a partial group.

city.description:
Find businesses in a specific city.

Accepts up to 32 values by repeating the parameter *(e.g. `city=value1&city=value2`)*.

Values cannot be comma separated here, as a comma can be part of the value. In the POST form, send an array instead.

name.description: Find businesses by their display name.

limit.description:
Maximum number of businesses to return.

**Allowed values:** `1-500`

state.description:
Find businesses in a specific state or province. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

US states match either way they are sent, by full name or by two-letter code.

cursor.description:
Pagination cursor for fetching the next page. Pass the `cursor` value returned in the previous response. Omit it on the first request.

**Note:** a cursor is only valid for the exact query that produced it, and it expires. Do not build or edit one.

fields.description:
A comma separated list of business fields to include in the response (field projection).

By default all fields are returned. `business_id` is always included.

**Note:** field projection trims the response body only. It does not change how the request is billed.

radius.description:
Radius of the area to search in, in meters.

**Allowed values:** `1-100000`

address.example: Office of City Treasurer, 121 N LaSalle St #106, Chicago, IL 60602
address.description: Find businesses by their full formatted address, including the business name.

country.description:
Find businesses in a specific country, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

For a list of supported country codes see *https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2*.

zipcode.description: Find businesses in a specific ZIP / postal code. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

district.description:
Find businesses in a specific district or neighbourhood, when the listing carries one.

Accepts up to 32 values by repeating the parameter *(e.g. `district=value1&district=value2`)*.

Values cannot be comma separated here, as a comma can be part of the value. In the POST form, send an array instead.

top_right.description:
The top-right (north-east) corner of the bounding box to search in, as a "lat,lng" string.

Send either bottom_left with top_right, or lat with lng and radius - not both, and not a partial group.

owner_name.description:
Find businesses by the name on the owner profile.

Accepts up to 32 values by repeating the parameter *(e.g. `owner_name=value1&owner_name=value2`)*.

Values cannot be comma separated here, as a comma can be part of the value. In the POST form, send an array instead.

bottom_left.description:
The bottom-left (south-west) corner of the bounding box to search in, as a "lat,lng" string.

Send either bottom_left with top_right, or lat with lng and radius - not both, and not a partial group.

business_id.description: Find businesses by their unique Business Id, matched exactly. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

phone_number.description:
Find businesses by phone number. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

Send the number with its country code, either in E.164 *(`+14325551234`, URL-encoded as `%2B14325551234`)* or in a decorated form such as `1-432-555-1234`, `(432) 555-1234` or `0014325551234`.

street_address.description:
Find businesses by the street line of their address on its own.

A single value is matched loosely, which also finds spelling and abbreviation variants. Several values are matched exactly instead, which narrows the result.

Accepts up to 32 values by repeating the parameter *(e.g. `street_address=value1&street_address=value2`)*.

Values cannot be comma separated here, as a comma can be part of the value. In the POST form, send an array instead.

business_category.description: Find businesses carrying a specific category. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

business_category_id.description:
Find businesses by Google's internal entity-type IDs. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

These are entity types rather than the listing's categories: the values are broad and a listing usually carries several of them, so this is a wide filter.

The IDs are gcids (Google Maps category IDs). For a list of gcids see *https://www.openwebninja.com/blog/all-google-maps-categories*.

main_business_category.description: Find businesses whose primary category matches. Same value space as the business_category parameter. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

main_business_category_id.description:
Find businesses by Google's internal ID of the primary category. Accepts a comma separated list of up to 32 values, or the parameter repeated up to 32 times (values are OR'ed).

This is the machine ID, not the display label the main_business_category parameter matches, and the two can name different primaries.

The IDs are gcids (Google Maps category IDs). For a list of gcids see *https://www.openwebninja.com/blog/all-google-maps-categories*.

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description:
Job Id of the job for which to get details. Batching of up to 20 Job Ids is supported by
separating multiple Job Ids by comma (,). The raw `job_uid` is also accepted. Each Job Id
in a batch counts as one request.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description:
Country code of the country the job was searched in, see ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. It is the
fallback for `job_country` when the job location names no country.

**Default:** `us`

parameters.name: language
parameters.description:
Language code sent to Bing with the request, see ISO 639-1. Leave empty to use the
primary language of `country`.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description:
Comma-separated projection over the job object, for example
`job_title,job_description,job_apply_link`. `job_id` and `job_title` are always
included, and every returned field can be selected. The search-only keys
(`job_position`, `job_bing_company_id`, `job_bing_title_id`) are accepted and ignored,
so one field list works on both endpoints. An unknown field name is a 400.

get.description:
Full details for up to 20 Bing job postings in one call, fetched concurrently, including
the complete job description and the decoded apply links of every board carrying the
posting.

**AI-extracted fields.** Each job is passed through the same AI enrichment as JSearch
`/job-details`, which adds `work_arrangement`, `seniority_level`,
`required_experience_years`, `education_required`, `visa_sponsorship`,
`relocation_required`, `relocation_assistance`, `contract_duration`, `start_date`,
`required_technologies`, `preferred_technologies`, `methodologies`, `industry`,
`job_function`, `has_management_responsibilities`, `ai_ml_involved`, `benefits_extended`
and `soft_skills`, and fills `job_min_salary`, `job_max_salary`, `job_salary_period`,
`job_city` and `job_state` where Bing left them empty. Results are cached for 7 days per
job. Enrichment is best-effort: if it fails, the job is returned without those fields.

`job_benefits_strings` is the full benefit list from the detail page; `/search` reports the
same list for the same job. `job_bing_company_id`, `job_bing_title_id` and `job_position`
are search-only.

An id this API did not mint, or a posting Bing no longer serves, is omitted from the array
while the rest of the batch resolves normally.

**Billing:** one request per requested id, including ids that do not resolve, so the cost
of a call is predictable before you make it.

data.description: Matching jobs in Bing's ranking order, de-duplicated by `job_id`. Empty when Bing has no matching jobs.

request_id.description: Unique id for this request, for tracing and support.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description:
Free-form job search query. Include the job title and location, for example
`developer jobs in new york`: Bing's jobs vertical is keyed off natural language, and a
bare keyword drifts toward unrelated postings. Exactly one `query` is accepted; a second
one is a 400.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description:
Free-text location, for example `New York, NY`. Appended to the `query` text, since
Bing builds its own location filter from coordinates. Putting the location inside
`query` works the same way.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
Page to return (each page includes up to 10 results). `page` + `num_pages` must stay
within page 50. Every request walks Bing's results from the start, so deeper pages take
longer.

**Default:** `1`

**Allowed values:** `1-50`

parameters.name: num_pages
parameters.description:
Number of pages to return, starting from `page`, merged and de-duplicated by `job_id`.
`page` + `num_pages` must stay within page 50. Each page of up to 10 results returned
consumes one request credit.

**Default:** `1`

**Allowed values:** `1-20`

parameters.name: country
parameters.description:
Country code of the country from which to return job postings, see ISO 3166-1
alpha-2. It selects Bing's national job index, so to search for developer jobs in
Berlin, send `country=de`.

**Default:** `us`

parameters.name: language
parameters.description:
Language code for Bing's interface language, see ISO 639-1. Leave empty to use the
primary language of `country`. With `en`, the word *jobs* is appended to a query that
does not already contain *job*.

parameters.name: date_posted
parameters.description:
Find jobs posted within the time you specify. `today`, `3days` and `week` are Bing's own
date filter. `month` has no Bing equivalent, since Bing's widest window is 7 days, so it
is sent unfiltered and returns a superset.

**Default:** `all`

**Allowed values:** `all`, `today`, `3days`, `week`, `month`

parameters.name: employment_types
parameters.description:
Find jobs of particular employment types, specified as a comma delimited list.
`FULLTIME`, `CONTRACTOR` and `PARTTIME` are filtered by Bing. `INTERN` has no Bing
filter and is enforced locally on the type Bing states. An unknown value is a 400.

**Allowed values:** `FULLTIME`, `CONTRACTOR`, `PARTTIME`, `INTERN`

parameters.name: work_from_home
parameters.description:
Only return work from home / remote jobs. Applied by Bing's own remote filter.

**Default:** `false`

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description:
Return jobs within a certain distance from the location in `query` or `location`, in
km. Bing honours only a 10 / 20 / 30 / 40 mile menu, so the value is converted to miles
and snapped to the nearest: 32 km becomes 20 miles.

parameters.name: exclude_job_publishers
parameters.description:
Exclude jobs published by specific publishers, as a comma separated list, for example
`LinkedIn,Indeed`. Bing has no publisher filter, so this is applied after fetching,
case-insensitively and as a substring match against `job_publisher` and every
`job_publishers` entry. A page can then return fewer than 10 jobs.

parameters.name: include_descriptions
parameters.description:
Whether to include the full job description and apply links. Bing search results carry
neither, so each job's detail page is fetched in parallel, capped at 100 jobs per
request. Set to `false` for a faster listing-only response. The detail fetches are not
billed.

**Default:** `true`

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description:
Comma-separated projection over the job object, for example
`job_title,employer_name,job_apply_link`. `job_id` and `job_title` are always included.
Every field this endpoint returns can be selected, including `job_location`,
`job_posted_at`, `job_publishers`, `job_employment_types`, `job_benefits_strings`,
`job_normalized_title` and `job_position`. An unknown field name is a 400.

get.description:
Search Bing's jobs vertical, with `date_posted`, `employment_types`, `work_from_home`,
`radius` and `exclude_job_publishers` filters.

**Query style matters.** Bing's vertical is keyed off natural language, so include the
role and the location in `query` (`developer jobs in new york`). A bare keyword drifts
toward unrelated postings. When `language` is `en` and the query does not already contain
*job*, the word *jobs* is appended automatically.

**`include_descriptions` defaults to `true`.** Bing's search cards carry no description and
no apply link, so for every result the job's detail page is fetched in parallel and
`job_description`, `job_apply_link`, `apply_options` and `employer_logo` are filled from it,
capped at 100 jobs per request. `job_benefits_strings` is taken from the detail page
whenever it parses, because the card shows only the first few chips and closes the row with
a *+N* overflow token, so `/search` and `/job-details` report the same benefits for the
same `job_id`. Measured on a
10-job page: 5.7 seconds and 69 KB with descriptions, 1.8 seconds and 13 KB with
`include_descriptions=false`.

**Pagination** is offset-based via `page` / `num_pages`, 10 jobs per page. Results merged
across `num_pages` are de-duplicated by `job_id`. Every request walks Bing's result list
from the start, so deeper pages take longer, and the walk stops once Bing starts repeating
postings already returned.

**Reliability.** The first Bing page is fetched from several exits concurrently and the
fullest answer wins, because Bing serves its *no jobs* page to some exits for a query
other exits answer normally. An empty `data` array therefore means Bing genuinely had no
matches; a failure to reach Bing is a `503`, and is not billed.

**Billing:** one request per page of 10 jobs returned, and at least one, so
`Requests` = 1 + (pages returned - 1), counted before `exclude_job_publishers` is applied.
The detail fetches behind `include_descriptions` are not billed. Both counts are visible in
the `X-RapidAPI-Billing` header.

get.description:
Search Bing Shopping for products across stores, with Bing's own price sort and price
range filters.

Each product carries its price as displayed and parsed, sale and shipping badges, rating,
the store and its product page, and a `product_id` to pass to `/product-details`.
Products from Bing's paid product grid are returned separately, in `sponsored_products`.
On some markets, such as Japan, Brazil and Canada, Bing often shows only that grid.

**Pagination.** Bing serves up to about 180 products per query. Most markets show 36
products per page, so pages 1 to 5 hold results; markets and queries where Bing uses its
list layout show 20 per page, up to page 9. A page past the end returns a `200` with
empty arrays.

**Market and language.** `country` sets the stores, prices and currency. Bing Shopping
serves `language=en` and the market's own language; a combination it does not serve,
such as `country=us&language=es`, returns a 400, as does a country without Bing Shopping.

**Billing:** one request per call.

Accepts a comma-separated list of values like `free_returns`, `deals_and_savings`, `returns_accepted`, `authorized_seller`, `sold_items`, `completed_items`, `free_shipping`, `local_pickup`. Example: `sold_items,completed_items`. Note: `sold_items` and `completed_items` work without a cookie, and the optional `cookie` parameter adds seller details to those results.

parameters.name: aspects
parameters.description:
Filter by category-specific item aspects from eBay's left-side filter panel (Brand, Model, Storage Capacity, Network, Color, etc.). Pass a JSON-encoded array of `{name, value}` objects. `value` can be a single string or an array of strings (multiple values are OR-joined within the same aspect).

Aspect names must match eBay's filter labels exactly. Aspects are scoped to the `category_id` you pass. The category determines which aspects are available. Common examples include: `Brand`, `Model`, `Storage Capacity`, `Network`, `Lock Status`, `Color`, `RAM`, `Screen Size`, `Operating System`, `Material`, `Size`, `Type`, `Features`.

**Limit:** up to 20 aspect entries per request.

**Examples:**
`[{"name":"Brand","value":"Samsung"}]`
`[{"name":"Storage Capacity","value":["128 GB","256 GB"]}]`
`[{"name":"Brand","value":"Samsung"},{"name":"Color","value":"Black"}]`

parameters.name: cookie
parameters.description:
Optional. Only used for **sold** and **completed** listings (`show_only=sold_items` / `completed_items`), ignored everywhere else.

Sold and completed listings are returned **without** a cookie: 60 results per page with the sale price, currency, sale date (`caption`), condition, shipping, location and images. On those results `seller_name`, `seller_feedback_count` and `seller_feedback_percentage` are `null` unless you pass your own eBay session cookie, which populates them on every result.

Paste the cookie header from a browser signed in to eBay, e.g. `name=value; name2=value2`. It must belong to the same marketplace as `domain`. If it stops working, because it expired, was signed out elsewhere, or belongs to another marketplace, the request returns 503 telling you to replace it rather than silently falling back. It is never logged or returned in the response.

More details: https://www.openwebninja.com/blog/how-to-get-ebay-sold-and-completed-listings

parameters.name: company

parameters.name: num_pages

budget is 90 s.

Review ordering, applied by Indeed. `relevance` (default) is Indeed's own order, which is
already newest-first. `helpfulness` puts most-helpful first. `rating_desc` and `rating_asc`

Narrow to one location within the selected country, in Indeed's own format (`Coopersburg,
PA`). **Requires a 2-letter `country`.** Indeed ignores this filter without one, so
sending it alone returns a 400 error.

Return only reviews that discuss one topic. The ids and their per-company review
counts and ratings are returned in `company_review_topics`. A value outside this set

get.description:
Employee reviews for one company, with its overall rating, the five category ratings
and the 1-5 star distribution.

Pass a job's `job_indeed_company_page_url` straight through as `company` to go from a
job to its employer's reviews in one hop.

**Transport.** The same one the job endpoints use - `curl_cffi` with Chrome
impersonation over the datacenter proxy ladder, anonymous throughout. Burn-tested
2026-09-11: 20 sequential requests across 10 companies and 3 page
offsets returned 20/20 HTTP 200 with parsed reviews, median 2.86 s (min 1.74 s,
max 5.79 s). Unlike Indeed's job SERP, this surface has **no page-2 sign-in wall** -
`start=240` was verified to return genuine page 13 anonymously.

**Envelope.** `data` is an OBJECT: company identity and aggregates alongside a
`reviews` array, mirroring Real-Time Amazon Data's `/product-reviews`.

**Two review counts, and they differ.** Indeed's default view is scoped to one country.
`company_review_count` is every review the company has; `company_filtered_review_count`
is how many the current filters can page through. Pass `country=ALL` to make them equal.

**Paging past the end.** Indeed silently serves **page 1 again** for a `start` well past
the last page (verified: `start=300`, `500`, `1000` all returned page 1's exact review
ids on a 260-review company). Those rows are detected via the page number Indeed echoes
and **discarded** - you get an empty `reviews` array and `parameters.page_past_last:
true`.

**Billing.** `Requests` counts one per upstream reviews page of 20, plus one more when
`company` was a free-text name that had to be resolved to a slug.

Fetch full details for up to 20 jobs in a single request. Indeed resolves the whole
batch in one upstream call (measured: 5 jobs in 761 ms), so a multi-id request costs
the same as a single-id one.

The job objects returned here carry the same fields as `/search` results, with

parameters.name: query
parameters.description:

a multi-valued `query` returns a 400 error.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description:
Where to search, in Indeed's own format, e.g. `New York, NY`, `London`,
`Berlin`. Omit to search the whole market.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number. 10 jobs per page. Values above 50 are clamped to 50.

parameters.name: num_pages
parameters.description:
How many pages to return in one response. A full job runs about 12 KB,
so beyond roughly 450 jobs the response is trimmed to fit the 6 MB limit and
`parameters.response_truncated` is set. You are billed only for pages returned. Pass
`fields` to keep a deep window intact.

parameters.name: country

ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 market code. Sent to Indeed as a header, so any market is
reachable regardless of the proxy exit country (verified US, GB, DE, CA, IN, AU).

parameters.name: language

parameters.name: date_posted
parameters.description:
Only return jobs posted within this window. `all` (the default) applies no date
filter. Combined with any other filter, the date window is applied locally and can
return fewer jobs than qualify; filter by date alone when you need every matching
job.

parameters.name: employment_types
parameters.description:
Comma-delimited list. A job matches if it carries **any** of the given types.
Indeed also tags Temporary and Seasonal, which have no enum member here and are
visible via `job_indeed_attributes`.

parameters.name: experience_level
parameters.description:
Comma-delimited list of seniority levels. A job matches if it carries **any** of
them. Enforced against Indeed's own seniority tags.

parameters.name: work_from_home
parameters.description:
When `true`, return only jobs Indeed tags as Remote. Hybrid roles are excluded;
see `job_indeed_is_hybrid` on the job object.

parameters.name: min_salary
parameters.description:
Minimum **annual** salary. Applied to the salary the employer actually stated,
annualised from `job_salary_period`. Jobs with no stated salary are excluded,
because they cannot be asserted to qualify.

parameters.name: max_salary
parameters.description: Maximum **annual** salary. Same semantics as `min_salary`.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description:
Search radius around `location`, in **kilometres**. Passed through to Indeed
exactly, so 2 returns jobs within 2 km. Values above 10000 are clamped.
**Requires `location`** - Indeed applies a radius only around a location, so
sending it alone returns a 400 error.

parameters.name: exclude_job_publishers
parameters.description:
Comma-delimited list of publishers to drop, matched case-insensitively against
`job_publisher`. Applied locally; Indeed has no upstream equivalent.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description:
Comma-delimited projection. Any key of the job object is valid; `job_id` and
`job_title` are always included. An unknown field is a 400.
Also the mechanism for pulling a deep result set in one call - see `num_pages`.

get.description:
Search LinkedIn job postings.

**Pagination** is offset-based via `page` / `num_pages`. Page size is fixed at 10 by LinkedIn. Unlike the Bing jobs source, LinkedIn does not repeat a posting across consecutive pages (measured: 300/300 unique ids over 30 contiguous pages), so `num_pages=N` returns exactly `N x 10` jobs up to the end of the result set.

**`include_details` (default `true`)** issues one extra request per job, bounded to 10 concurrent and capped at 100 jobs per request. It is what fills `job_description`, `job_employment_type(s)`, salary, `job_seniority_level`, `job_function`, `job_industries`, `job_applicants_count` and `job_linkedin_company_id` — none of which exist on a search card. Set it to `false` for a ~3x faster, card-only response.

**Knowing when to stop:** the response is a flat array, matching the JSearch `/search` envelope, so there is no `has_more` flag. A page that returns fewer than `num_pages x 10` jobs is the last one, as is `page` 100.

**Billing:** `Requests` counts one per upstream page of 10 actually fetched. Using `employment_types`, `seniority_levels` or `remote_jobs_only` over-fetches up to 3x the requested pages (capped at 10) to refill the page after local filtering, and those extra pages are billed.

get.description:
Every open Monster job posting at one or more employers.

This is the **same search path** as `/search` with Monster's `companyDisplayNames` filter
populated: the same fetch layer, the same parser, the same job builder, the same job
contract and the same `job_id` codec. `location`, `radius`, `country`, `date_posted`,
`employment_types`, `page`, `num_pages` and `fields` all behave exactly as they do on
`/search`.

**Identifying an employer.** Monster publishes no company id, so the match is on the
DISPLAY NAME, which is the string returned as `employer_name` on any job. `Genentech`
works, while a slug such as `genentech-inc`, a URL, or a misspelling returns nothing. It
is a SUBSTRING match, so a short name also reaches longer employers containing it
(`Lines` reaches `Melton Truck Lines` and `Florida Rock & Tank Lines`); pass the full
`employer_name` and it behaves as an exact match. The company filter is what finds them:
`query=Genentech` returned 0 rows where the company filter returned 7.

**A comma inside a name is safe.** The list separator is a comma and most US employer
names end in one (`Cross Country Healthcare, Inc.`). A trailing fragment that is only a
corporate suffix is rejoined to the name before it, so `Cross Country Healthcare, Inc.`
is one employer while `Genentech,Deloitte` is still two.

**Multiple employers are an OR.** Monster ranks the union by relevance, so a small
employer paired with a large one can be absent from page 1 entirely. What is guaranteed
is that every job returned belongs to one of the requested employers.

**`query` is optional here**, unlike on `/search`: the employer is the constraint. So is
`location`, so a caller can browse one employer country-wide.

**`sort_by`, `remote_jobs_only` and `language` are ignored on this endpoint.** Use
`/search` for those.

**An employer with no open jobs returns an empty array**, and so does a name Monster does
not recognise. With no id to validate against, the two cases are indistinguishable.

**Billing:** identical to `/search`. `Requests` counts one per upstream page of 10
actually fetched.

get.description:
Search Monster job postings by keyword, with the filters Monster honors server-side:
`location` with a kilometre `radius`, `country`, `date_posted` and `employment_types`.

**A search row already carries the whole job.** Description, salary, coordinates and the
apply URL are all on the search response.

**Pagination** is offset-based via `page` / `num_pages`, 10 jobs per page. Pages are
chained upstream: a full walk of the retrievable window at Monster's own maximum page
size returned 550 rows, 550 unique ids and zero duplicates.

**Retrieval ceiling: 510 postings per query.** Monster serves nothing past an upstream
offset of 500 and does so silently, with a 200 and an empty array, so `page` is capped
at 51 and `page` + `num_pages` may not cross it. This is independent of the much larger
estimated total Monster reports internally for the same query.

**Knowing when to stop:** the response is a flat array of jobs, and page 51 is the
last page. Short pages do occur inside the window, so a page of fewer than 10 jobs is
still a page in the middle of it.

**Billing:** `Requests` counts one per upstream page of 10 actually fetched. Two things
add to it, and both are visible in the `X-RapidAPI-Billing` header.
Any `page` above 1 costs **one extra request**: Monster ignores the offset on the first
call of a new search and serves the head of the list, so a deep start has to pin the
result set with a tiny lookup before it can page into it. That is one extra request no
matter how deep you start. And combining `remote_jobs_only` with `employment_types`
over-fetches up to 3x the requested pages (capped at 10) to refill the page after local
filtering, and those extra pages are billed too.

The news search query.

**Examples:**

parameters.description:
Page number for pagination. Each page returns up to 10 news results.

**Allowed values:** `1` and above.

parameters.description:
Country code of the country to return news results for. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2 for supported values.

parameters.name: time_period
parameters.description:
Filter results to a specific time period. Cannot be used together with `date_from`/`date_to`.

**Allowed values:** `any`, `last_hour`, `last_day`, `last_week`, `last_month`, `last_year`

parameters.description:

**Example:** `01/01/2026`

parameters.name: date_to
parameters.description:
End date for a custom date range filter, in `MM/DD/YYYY` format. Must be provided together with `date_from`.

**Example:** `04/10/2026`

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description:
Sort order for the results.

**Allowed values:** `relevance`, `date`

**Default:** `relevance`

parameters.name: safe
parameters.description:
Safe search setting to filter explicit content.

**Allowed values:** `off`, `active`

**Default:** `off`

get.description: Get real-time short video search results from across the web with pagination and filtering support.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description:
The video search query.

**Examples:**

`how to invest`

`product demo software`

`lebron james highlights`

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
Page number for pagination. Each page returns up to 10 video results.

**Allowed values:** `1` and above.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description:
Country code of the country to return video results for. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2 for supported values.

**Default:** `us`

parameters.name: language
parameters.description:
The language of the results, specified as a 2-letter language code - see ISO 639-1.

**Default:** `en`

parameters.name: time_period
parameters.description:
Filter results to a specific time period. Cannot be used together with `date_from`/`date_to`.

**Allowed values:** `any`, `last_hour`, `last_day`, `last_week`, `last_month`, `last_year`

**Default:** `any`

parameters.name: date_from
parameters.description:
Start date for a custom date range filter, in `MM/DD/YYYY` format. Must be provided together with `date_to`. Cannot be used together with `time_period` (other than `any`).

**Example:** `01/01/2026`

parameters.name: date_to
parameters.description:
End date for a custom date range filter, in `MM/DD/YYYY` format. Must be provided together with `date_from`.

**Example:** `04/29/2026`

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description:
Sort order for the results.

**Allowed values:** `relevance`, `date`

**Default:** `relevance`

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description:
Filter results by video duration.

**Allowed values:** `any`, `short` (under 4 minutes), `medium` (4 to 20 minutes), `long` (over 20 minutes)

**Default:** `any`

parameters.name: safe
parameters.description:
Safe search setting to filter explicit content.

**Allowed values:** `off`, `active`

**Default:** `off`

get.description: Search Google Videos for any query and get real-time video results. Returns video results with title, link, source info, thumbnail URL, duration (both human-readable string and seconds), and published dates (both localized relative text and ISO 8601 UTC), plus a list of related searches when available for the query. Supports pagination, filtering by time period or custom date range, video duration, country, language, sort order, and safe search.

get.description:
The pay distribution ZipRecruiter publishes for a job title, nationally or in one US state
or Canadian province. One upstream page, one row.

The row carries the house `/estimated-salary` contract keys, plus 18 `ziprecruiter_*`
extras.

**The median is the real median.** ZipRecruiter's own JSON-LD publishes a field labelled
`median` that is actually the MEAN: it was byte-identical to the page's average on 16 of 16
pages measured, and on Truck Driver it reads 56,348 against a true median of 49,500, which
is 13.8% high. Every scraper that reads the easy JSON-LD field ships that mean labelled as
a median. `median_salary` here is parsed out of the page's own data layer and is the real
median; ZipRecruiter's figure is carried alongside as `ziprecruiter_json_ld_median` so the
difference is auditable in the response itself.

**Figures are always annual** and `salary_period` is always `YEAR`.
ZipRecruiter leads 6 of 11 titles measured with an hourly figure, but its own structured
data is annual (`P1Y`) on 13 of 13 pages, including every hourly-preferring title. Driving
the row off the page's preference would make `median_salary` mean something different for
Truck Driver than for Data Scientist. All four frequencies ride along in
`ziprecruiter_pay_frequencies`, and the page's own preference is preserved as
`ziprecruiter_preferred_pay_period`.

**What only this source has:** p25 and p75, an 11-bucket salary histogram giving the real
distribution, a 59 to 64 row state and province table, the 10 top-paying cities, 5 related
titles with pay deltas, all four pay frequencies on one row, the count of open listings
behind the figures, the spread level, ZipRecruiter's own summary prose and its generated
FAQ.

**Coverage is national and state or province level only.** A city returns a 400 error
before any request is made: ZipRecruiter publishes salary pages at state and national
level. `location_type` and `years_of_experience`, which JSearch offers, return a 400 error
here.

A title ZipRecruiter has never published, or a title with no figures for the requested
state, returns a 404 error. Coverage is decided per title and state pair:
`Software-Engineer` has an Ontario page, `Truck-Driver` a national page only.

**Billing:** `Requests` counts 1 per call.

get.description:
Full details for up to 20 ZipRecruiter job postings in one call, fetched concurrently.

This endpoint always reads the detail surface, so the detail-only fields are filled without
any flag: `job_description` and `ziprecruiter_description_html` at 100%, `job_highlights`
at 72%, `job_onet_soc`, `ziprecruiter_job_industry` and `ziprecruiter_valid_through` at 73%
(ZipRecruiter ships JSON-LD on 73% of detail pages), `employer_website` and the company
widget fields at 54%, and `employer_reviews` at 14%.

Three fields belong to the search card and are `null` here:
`ziprecruiter_short_description`, the card teaser; `ziprecruiter_updated_at`,
ZipRecruiter's listing refresh stamp; and `ziprecruiter_is_new`, a card badge.

An id this API did not mint, or a posting ZipRecruiter has taken down, is omitted from the
array while the rest of the batch resolves normally. A request made entirely of ids from
another job API returns a 200 with an empty array.

**Billing:** `Requests` counts one per requested id, including ids that turn out to be
foreign, so the cost of a call is predictable before you make it.

get.description:
Search ZipRecruiter job postings by keyword, with the filters ZipRecruiter honors
server-side: `location` with a kilometre `radius`, `date_posted`, `employment_types`,
`experience_level`, `salary_min` / `salary_max`, `remote_jobs_only`, `zipapply_only` and
`company_id`.

**`include_details` defaults to `false`, and this is the single most important thing to
understand about this endpoint.** A ZipRecruiter search card carries a roughly
200-character teaser and nothing more. `job_description`, `job_highlights`,
`employer_website`, `employer_reviews`, `job_onet_soc`, `ziprecruiter_description_html`,
`ziprecruiter_job_industry`, `ziprecruiter_valid_through`, `ziprecruiter_ats_identifier`,
`ziprecruiter_company_size`, `ziprecruiter_company_hq`, `ziprecruiter_company_industries`,
`ziprecruiter_key_responsibilities` and `ziprecruiter_employer_faq` are all detail-only and
come back `null` on a plain search. Set `include_details=true` to fill them. The teaser is
always published separately as `ziprecruiter_short_description`, so a card-only response
still carries usable copy.

Filling the details costs one extra upstream request per job, which is why it is opt-in.
With `include_details=true`, `num_pages` may be at most 5, which is 100 jobs; a larger
value returns a 400 error.

**Pagination** is 20 jobs per page. The ceiling is `ceil(total_results / 20)`, where
`total_results` is ZipRecruiter's own count of matches, and the largest result set observed
was 946 jobs. Duplicates ZipRecruiter repeats across adjacent pages are removed, so a page
may yield fewer than 20 new jobs. The response is a flat array, so a call returning fewer
than `num_pages` x 20 jobs is how you know you have reached the end of the result set.

**Scoping to one company** is what `company_id` is for, and the value is the
`ziprecruiter_company_id` carried on every job. ZipRecruiter fails this filter OPEN in two
ways, both silent: a bad id returns the full unfiltered search, and a valid one
intermittently drops the filter. Send `location` alongside `company_id`: that is what keeps
the drop rare. Measured on one id with five interleaved repeats per arm, the filter held
5/5 with a location and 1/5 without, and the misses returned 6, 4 and 20 distinct
employers. So every returned card is checked against the requested id, a page that fails
the check is refetched, and an id that stays unscoped returns a 404 error.
`total_results` is omitted for a company-scoped search: ZipRecruiter's count there swings
from 1 to 540 across 20 identical calls. Note that roughly a third of postings carry the
placeholder id `zr_missing_company_default`, ZipRecruiter's marker for a posting whose
company record is missing; it returns a 404 error here, so pick an id off a job whose
`employer_name` is the company you want.

**Sorting.** Results come back in ZipRecruiter's own relevance order. `sort_by`, `sort`,
`order` and a `company` NAME each return a 400 error, because ZipRecruiter accepts and
then ignores them.

**Billing:** `Requests` counts one per requested SERP page, plus one per detail page when

field blank.

| field | fill |

| `review_country` `review_is_current_employee` `review_status` `review_is_redacted` | 140/140 |
| `review_posted_at` + all three parsed date fields | 140/140 |
| `review_helpful_count` `review_unhelpful_count` `review_comment_count` | 140/140 |
| `review_url` `review_share_url` | 140/140 |
| `review_job_title` | 103/140 |
| `review_job_title_normalized` | 101/140 |
| `review_location` | 86/140 |
| `review_category_ratings` (each of the five) | 52-54/140 |

The category ratings are sparse **because Indeed lets a reviewer rate overall only**, not
because extraction is unreliable: they are populated or null as a group of five.

job_position.description: Absolute 1-based rank of the job within the full result set for this query. Null on /job-details, which has no notion of rank.

apply_options.description: Application routes. Indeed exposes exactly one source per posting, so this array holds 0 or 1 entries.

employer_logo.description: Square employer logo. From Indeed's employer dossier (69% of 600 measured jobs); where Indeed has none, a Google faviconV2 URL derived from the employer website or apply domain is substituted. Null only when neither is available.

job_is_remote.description: True when the posting carries Indeed's "Remote" attribute. Hybrid roles are false here and true on job_indeed_is_hybrid.

job_posted_at.description: Relative posting age in the JSearch vocabulary: "today", "N days ago" up to 30, then "N month(s) ago". Derived from job_posted_at_timestamp.

job_publisher.description: Who is serving the application: the employer/ATS host derived from the apply URL, mapped to a friendly name for known ATSs (Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, iCIMS, ...).

job_apply_link.description: Direct application URL. On Indeed this is the employer's own careers page or ATS, not an Indeed redirect - populated on 600/600 measured jobs.

job_highlights.description: Always an empty object. Indeed ships one flat description with no qualifications/responsibilities/benefits split, so there is nothing to structure. Present for shape parity with the Google-backed surface.

job_max_salary.description: Upper salary bound in the units of job_salary_period. Null when unstated or when only a lower bound was given.

job_min_salary.description: Lower salary bound in the units of job_salary_period. Null when unstated or when only an upper bound was given.

job_description.description: Full plain-text job description, returned in the SEARCH response. See job_description_html for the markup.

job_google_link.description: Always null. Google-for-Jobs specific and not applicable to an Indeed-sourced posting.

employer_reviews.description: Always null here. Indeed publishes its company rating and review count on the /cmp company surface. GET /company-reviews returns them with the full review list, the category ratings and the 1-5 star distribution, at one request per 20 reviews. Pass job_indeed_company_page_url from any job here as the company parameter.

employer_website.description: Employer's corporate website (72% of 600 measured jobs).

job_salary_period.description: Unit the salary bounds are expressed in: YEAR, MONTH, WEEK, DAY or HOUR. Salary values keep the unit the employer stated.

job_indeed_ref_num.description: The employer's own requisition id, e.g. "JR2025219". 100% coverage.

job_apply_is_direct.description: True when job_apply_link points at the employer/ATS rather than at another job board.

job_indeed_language.description: ISO 639-1 language of the posting as detected by Indeed.

job_description_html.description: The job description with Indeed's original HTML markup preserved.

job_indeed_attributes.description: Every attribute Indeed tagged on the posting - 27 to 66 per job, mixing skills, employment type, seniority, benefits and work arrangement. The SUIDs here are the same tokens the employment_types / experience_level / work_from_home filters use upstream.

job_indeed_employer_key.description: Indeed's stable company identifier (96% coverage). Also the encodedFccId used by the /cmp company pages.

job_posted_at_timestamp.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of when the posting appeared on Indeed. 100% coverage.

job_indeed_is_urgent_hire.description: True when Indeed flags the posting as urgently hiring.

job_published_at_timestamp.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of the employer's own publish date. Distinct from job_posted_at_timestamp, which is when the posting reached Indeed.

job_indeed_company_page_url.description: Absolute URL of the employer's Indeed company page, e.g. "https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Capgemini".

job_indeed_normalized_title.description: Indeed's normalized job title, e.g. "devops engineer".

job_indeed_employer_industry.description: Industry from the Indeed company dossier (13% coverage).

job_indeed_experience_levels.description: Seniority tags on the posting: ENTRY_LEVEL, MID_LEVEL, SENIOR_LEVEL and/or NO_EXPERIENCE. Empty array when Indeed tagged none.

job_indeed_source_employer_name.description: Employer name as it appeared on the source feed, before Indeed matched it to a company record.

jobs_omitted.description:
Matching jobs dropped to fit the payload limit. Present only when
`response_truncated` is `true`. You are not billed for these.

jobs_returned.description: Jobs in `data`. Present only when `response_truncated` is `true`.

response_truncated.description:
`true` when the response was trimmed to stay inside the 6 MB service payload limit,
and some jobs that matched were therefore not returned. Always present.

This is a statement about the RESPONSE, not about the source: it does not mean
Indeed ran out of jobs. A short response with `response_truncated: false` means the
cursor was exhausted; a short response with `response_truncated: true` means we could

sds_L_Fsr74jXxRwFrRFUiukT_7bc4ac4354ea13.description:
Echo of the parameters as the caller sent them, before any internal normalisation.
`date_posted: all` is echoed verbatim even though it is applied as "no date filter".
Keys the caller did not send are absent.

Three keys are NOT an echo but a report on the response itself:
`response_truncated`, and - only when it is `true` - `jobs_returned` and `jobs_omitted`.

job_id.description: Stable, opaque job identifier: base64url("indeed:" + the Indeed job key). Pass this to /job-details. Always present.

job_uid.description: The raw 16-hex Indeed job key that job_id encodes. Stable and valid indefinitely.

job_state.description: State / province / admin-1 code, e.g. "NY". 100% coverage.

job_title.description: Job title as posted by the employer.

job_salary.description: Single headline salary figure: the midpoint of the stated range, or the single stated bound. Null when the employer stated no salary.

job_country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Resolved from Indeed's country name, which is localised per market ("Deutschland" for de-DE), and falls back to the requested `country` when unrecognised. Always a 2-letter code.

job_benefits.description: Always null. The normalized JSearch benefit enum has no Indeed equivalent; the raw benefit labels are in job_benefits_strings.

job_location.description: Full formatted location, e.g. "New York, NY 10003".

job_onet_soc.description: Always null. Indeed's occupations[] are its own SUID taxonomy, not O*NET SOC codes; they are exposed verbatim as job_indeed_occupations.

job_position.description: Absolute 1-based rank of the job within the full result set for this query. Null on /job-details, which has no notion of rank.

apply_options.description: Application routes. Indeed exposes exactly one source per posting, so this array holds 0 or 1 entries.

employer_logo.description: Square employer logo. From Indeed's employer dossier (69% of 600 measured jobs); where Indeed has none, a Google faviconV2 URL derived from the employer website or apply domain is substituted. Null only when neither is available.

employer_name.description: Employer name. Falls back to Indeed's `sourceEmployerName` when the employer record is absent. Populated on 100% of measured jobs.

job_is_remote.description: True when the posting carries Indeed's "Remote" attribute. Hybrid roles are false here and true on job_indeed_is_hybrid.

job_posted_at.description: Relative posting age in the JSearch vocabulary: "today", "N days ago" up to 30, then "N month(s) ago". Derived from job_posted_at_timestamp.

job_publisher.description: Who is serving the application: the employer/ATS host derived from the apply URL, mapped to a friendly name for known ATSs (Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, iCIMS, ...).

job_apply_link.description: Direct application URL. On Indeed this is the employer's own careers page or ATS, not an Indeed redirect - populated on 600/600 measured jobs.

job_highlights.description: Always an empty object. Indeed ships one flat description with no qualifications/responsibilities/benefits split, so there is nothing to structure. Present for shape parity with the Google-backed surface.

job_max_salary.description: Upper salary bound in the units of job_salary_period. Null when unstated or when only a lower bound was given.

job_min_salary.description: Lower salary bound in the units of job_salary_period. Null when unstated or when only an upper bound was given.

job_description.description: Full plain-text job description, returned in the SEARCH response. See job_description_html for the markup.

job_google_link.description: Always null. Google-for-Jobs specific and not applicable to an Indeed-sourced posting.

employer_reviews.description: Always null here. Indeed publishes its company rating and review count on the /cmp company surface. GET /company-reviews returns them with the full review list, the category ratings and the 1-5 star distribution, at one request per 20 reviews. Pass job_indeed_company_page_url from any job here as the company parameter.

employer_website.description: Employer's corporate website (72% of 600 measured jobs).

job_salary_period.description: Unit the salary bounds are expressed in: YEAR, MONTH, WEEK, DAY or HOUR. Salary values keep the unit the employer stated.

job_salary_string.description: Salary exactly as Indeed renders it, e.g. "$152,000 - $221,000 a year" (60% of measured jobs).

job_indeed_expired.description: True when Indeed has marked the posting expired.

job_indeed_ref_num.description: The employer's own requisition id, e.g. "JR2025219". 100% coverage.

job_apply_is_direct.description: True when job_apply_link points at the employer/ATS rather than at another job board.

job_employment_type.description: Primary employment type. One of FULLTIME, CONTRACTOR, PARTTIME, INTERN. Null when Indeed tagged none of them.

job_indeed_language.description: ISO 639-1 language of the posting as detected by Indeed.

job_benefits_strings.description: Benefit labels as Indeed states them, e.g. "401(k)", "Health insurance", "Paid time off". Null when the posting lists none.

job_description_html.description: The job description with Indeed's original HTML markup preserved.

job_employment_types.description: All employment types tagged on the posting, in the enum order FULLTIME, CONTRACTOR, PARTTIME, INTERN. Empty array when Indeed tagged none. Indeed also uses Temporary and Seasonal tags, which have no JSearch enum member and are exposed only in job_indeed_attributes rather than being folded into CONTRACTOR.

job_indeed_is_hybrid.description: True when the posting carries Indeed's "Hybrid work" attribute.

job_indeed_attributes.description: Every attribute Indeed tagged on the posting - 27 to 66 per job, mixing skills, employment type, seniority, benefits and work arrangement. The SUIDs here are the same tokens the employment_types / experience_level / work_from_home filters use upstream.

job_indeed_occupations.description: Indeed's occupation taxonomy for the posting.

job_indeed_employer_key.description: Indeed's stable company identifier (96% coverage). Also the encodedFccId used by the /cmp company pages.

job_posted_at_timestamp.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of when the posting appeared on Indeed. 100% coverage.

job_indeed_is_urgent_hire.description: True when Indeed flags the posting as urgently hiring.

job_published_at_timestamp.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of the employer's own publish date. Distinct from job_posted_at_timestamp, which is when the posting reached Indeed.

job_indeed_company_page_url.description: Absolute URL of the employer's Indeed company page, e.g. "https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Capgemini".

job_indeed_normalized_title.description: Indeed's normalized job title, e.g. "devops engineer".

job_indeed_employer_industry.description: Industry from the Indeed company dossier (13% coverage).

job_indeed_experience_levels.description: Seniority tags on the posting: ENTRY_LEVEL, MID_LEVEL, SENIOR_LEVEL and/or NO_EXPERIENCE. Empty array when Indeed tagged none.

job_indeed_source_employer_name.description: Employer name as it appeared on the source feed, before Indeed matched it to a company record.

job_indeed_employer_header_image.description: Employer banner image from the Indeed company dossier (54% coverage).

job_indeed_is_high_volume_hiring.description: True when Indeed flags the posting as high-volume hiring.

job_function.description: LinkedIn's job-function label. Detail surface only.

job_latitude.description: Always `null`; not published on this surface.

job_is_remote.description: `true` or `null`, **never `false`**. LinkedIn's logged-out payload has no workplace-type field, so `true` is emitted only when an explicit textual remote marker is present and `null` means "LinkedIn did not say", not "not remote". 0/50 on the measured sample.

job_longitude.description: Always `null`; not published on this surface.

job_posted_at_date.description: The exact `datetime` attribute LinkedIn publishes on a search card. **Search surface only** — always `null` on `/job-details`, which carries no date element.

job_apply_is_direct.description: Always `false`; the employer's own application destination is not visible.

job_salary_currency.description: ISO 4217 code inferred from the salary string's symbol or code.

job_seniority_level.description: LinkedIn's own seniority vocabulary. Detail surface only.

job_benefits_strings.description: Always `null`. LinkedIn's only chips are engagement badges ("Actively Hiring"), which are not benefits; they are returned as `job_linkedin_badges` instead.

job_employment_types.description: Normalized enum form of `job_employment_type`. Empty when `include_details=false`.

page.description: The page the response starts at. Always present, defaulting to 1.

query.description: The keyword filter as sent. Absent when the employer was the only constraint.

radius.description: The radius in kilometres, as sent.

company.description: The employer display names exactly as sent, trimmed.

country.description: The country code as sent, lowercased. Absent when it defaulted to `us`.

location.description: The location exactly as sent. Absent when the search was country-wide.

num_pages.description: How many pages were fetched. Always present, defaulting to 1.

date_posted.description: The freshness window exactly as sent, `all` included.

employment_types.description: The employment types exactly as sent, before uppercasing and splitting.

sds_L_Fsr74jXxRwFrRFUiukT_59a9ba9486dc24.description: Echo of the parameters as the caller sent them. `query` is absent when none was sent, since it is optional on this endpoint. `page` and `num_pages` are always echoed with the value actually used.

job_id.description: Opaque public id for the posting, `base64url("monster:" + <Monster job uuid>)`. Pass it back to `/job-details`. Stable for the life of the posting.

job_uid.description: Monster's own job id, a permanent UUIDv4. Accepted directly by `/job-details` and the right key for a downstream cache.

job_city.description: City. `null` on a country-level or region-only posting.

job_state.description: The full state or province NAME, matching JSearch. The code appears inside `job_location`.

job_title.description: The job title as Monster publishes it.

job_salary.description: Set only when a posting states ONE figure rather than a range, in the unit given by `job_salary_period`. A range populates `job_min_salary` / `job_max_salary` instead.

job_seo_id.description: The slugged id from the public posting URL, `<slugified title>-<city>-<state>--<uuid>`. Accepted by `/job-details` in place of the uuid, so a caller holding only a scraped URL can round-trip with it.

job_skills.description: Monster's knowledge-base skill tags for the posting, deduplicated and capped at 40. These are short tags, one concept each.

job_status.description: The posting's lifecycle status. `ACTIVE` on every posting measured, and the field that reports the change when Monster pulls a posting.

job_country.description: Uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, taken from the posting's own address where it names one and falling back to the requested `country`.

job_benefits.description: Monster's normalized benefit enum, lowercased to snake_case so the shape matches JSearch's own keys. Rare: most Monster postings are syndicated feeds with no benefits block. `null` when none are stated.

job_industry.description: The industry Monster assigns to the posting. Present on a minority of postings.

job_latitude.description: Latitude of the job location, as Monster publishes it.

job_location.description: Display location, `"City, ST"` for US postings and `"City, ST, CC"` elsewhere. Falls back to the country code alone on a posting with no city or region.

job_onet_soc.description: The O*NET-SOC occupation code as an 8-digit string with no punctuation, matching the rest of the fleet. The human title is published separately as `job_occupational_category`.

job_position.description: 0-based rank of the job within the upstream page it came from. Rank restarts at 0 on each page, so it orders one page at a time. Always `null` on `/job-details`, which has no result set to rank within.

job_provider.description: The upstream feed that delivered this posting to Monster, for example JobTarget, Jobot or Appcast. Provenance only; `job_publisher` is always `Monster`.

apply_options.description: Ways to apply, most authoritative first. One entry on most postings, two when Monster also exposes the destination its apply URL redirects to. Empty only when Monster publishes no usable URL at all.

employer_logo.description: The employer's logo. Monster's own CDN supplies it on about 30% of postings; for most of the rest it is resolved from the employer's own domain.

employer_name.description: The hiring employer's name. This is the string `/company-jobs` matches on.

employer_size.description: Employee headcount band from the employer's branding block.

job_is_remote.description: Whether the job can be done remotely. A real tri-state: `true` when Monster marks the posting `REMOTE` or `ONSITE_AND_REMOTE`, `false` only when it explicitly says `ONSITE`, and `null` when Monster did not say, which is the common case.

job_longitude.description: Longitude of the job location, as Monster publishes it.

location.description:

job_title.description:

`Registered Nurse` resolves to `RN`. What was sent is echoed in `parameters`, and the
page's own raw title is `ziprecruiter_job_title_searched`.

confidence.description:
