describes how widely the top-city figures spread, which is a different thing.

max_salary.description: 90th percentile annual pay, the top of the middle 80%.

min_salary.description: 10th percentile annual pay, the bottom of the middle 80%.

salary_count.description:
Always `null`. ZipRecruiter states no sample size for its estimate. The count of open
postings behind the page is a different quantity and is published as
`ziprecruiter_total_listings`.

median_salary.description:
The real annual median, parsed from the page's own data layer. The JSON-LD field
labelled `median` is the mean and reads up to 13.8% high; it is carried separately as
`ziprecruiter_json_ld_median`.

salary_period.description:
Always `YEAR`. ZipRecruiter's own structured data is annual on every page measured,
including titles the page leads with an hourly figure, so annual keeps titles
comparable. The other frequencies are in `ziprecruiter_pay_frequencies`.

publisher_link.description:
The ZipRecruiter salary page these figures were read from, so any number on the row can
be checked against its source.

publisher_name.description: Always `ZipRecruiter`. Constant by construction on this source.

max_base_salary.description: Always `null`, for the same reason as `min_base_salary`.

min_base_salary.description:
Always `null`. ZipRecruiter publishes total pay only on this surface, with no
base-versus-additional split.

salary_currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency of every figure on the row, from the page's own country field. `USD`
for US pages, `CAD` for Canadian ones.

ziprecruiter_faq.description:
ZipRecruiter's generated FAQ for this title and scope, typically 3 entries covering the
headline figure, the best-paying related titles and the top-paying cities. An empty
array when the page carries none.

max_additional_pay.description: Always `null`, for the same reason as `min_additional_pay`.

median_base_salary.description: Always `null`, for the same reason as `min_base_salary`.

min_additional_pay.description:
Always `null`. ZipRecruiter states total pay only, with no bonus, commission or equity
component broken out.

salaries_updated_at.description:
ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the date ZipRecruiter last refreshed the figures. The raw
text it prints is kept as `ziprecruiter_salaries_updated_at_text`.

ziprecruiter_summary.description:
ZipRecruiter's own prose summary of the figures, HTML stripped to plain text. Ready to
show to an end user without writing the sentence yourself.

median_additional_pay.description: Always `null`, for the same reason as `min_additional_pay`.

ziprecruiter_p25_salary.description: 25th percentile annual pay. With p75 it gives the interquartile range.

ziprecruiter_spread_level.description:
How widely the top-city figures spread: `large`, `medium` or `small`. ZipRecruiter's
own label.

ziprecruiter_average_salary.description:
The annual MEAN, published under its real name. It differs from `median_salary` on
every title measured.

ziprecruiter_json_ld_median.description:
The figure ZipRecruiter's own JSON-LD labels `median`, carried so the discrepancy is
auditable. It is the MEAN: byte-identical to the page average on 16 of 16 pages
measured, and on Truck Driver it reads 56,348 against a true median of 49,500, 13.8%
high. Compare it to `median_salary`.

ziprecruiter_related_titles.description:
The 5 related titles ZipRecruiter lists, each with its pay delta against the searched
title. Every one can be fed straight back into `job_title`.

ziprecruiter_total_listings.description:
How many open ZipRecruiter postings sit behind this page right now. A demand signal
for the title, separate from the estimate's sample size. `0` is a real answer.

ziprecruiter_pay_frequencies.description:
All four pay frequencies in one response, each with its own full distribution. Read
`hour` for an hourly role without a second request and without dividing an annual
figure by an assumed number of hours.

ziprecruiter_salaries_by_state.description:
Pay for this title in every US state and Canadian province ZipRecruiter has figures
for, 59 to 64 rows. National requests only: an empty array on a state request.

ziprecruiter_top_paying_cities.description:
The 10 highest-paying cities for this title, across the country on a national request
and within the state on a state request.

ziprecruiter_job_title_searched.description:
The page's own raw title, before ZipRecruiter's canonicalisation. `Registered Nurse`
where `job_title` reads `RN`.

ziprecruiter_location_granularity.description:
Which page answered: `NATIONAL` or `STATE`. Read from the page's own scope field, so it

ziprecruiter_preferred_pay_period.description:
The frequency ZipRecruiter itself leads the page with: `HOUR` on 6 of 11 titles

ziprecruiter_national_average_salary.description:
The national annual mean for this title. Equal to `ziprecruiter_average_salary` on a
national request; the benchmark a state figure is above or below on a state request.

ziprecruiter_salaries_updated_at_text.description:
The refresh date exactly as ZipRecruiter prints it. The parsed form is

job_id.description:
Stable, opaque id for this posting. Pass it straight back to `/job-details`. Encodes
ZipRecruiter's own seat id, so it survives re-fetches and is the same on every surface.

job_uid.description:
ZipRecruiter's own raw seat id, 16 hex characters. Stable across surfaces and
re-fetches, accepted directly by `/job-details`, and the right key for an enrichment
cache.

job_city.description: City. `null` on a state-level or remote-only listing.

job_state.description:
The full state or province NAME, matching JSearch. The two-letter code appears inside
`job_location`.

job_title.description: The job title as ZipRecruiter publishes it. 100% fill.

job_salary.description:
The headline salary figure: the midpoint when the posting states a range, the single
bound otherwise, in the period given by `job_salary_period`. 69% fill. Populated only
when ZipRecruiter itself displays the pay.

job_country.description: Uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. `US` or `CA` on this source.

job_benefits.description:
Normalised benefit tags ZipRecruiter states on the posting. 44% fill; `null` when none
are stated.

job_latitude.description:
Always `null`. ZipRecruiter publishes coordinates on neither the card, the detail
payload nor the JSON-LD.

job_location.description: The location as ZipRecruiter displays it on the posting. 100% fill.

job_onet_soc.description:
The O*NET-SOC occupation code ZipRecruiter states, with the human title removed.
Detail surface only, and capped at 73% because it comes from JSON-LD, which
ZipRecruiter ships on 73% of detail pages.

apply_options.description:
Ways to apply. ZipRecruiter exposes exactly one, its own posting page, so this is a
one-entry array, or empty on the rare job with no resolvable URL.

employer_logo.description:
The employer's logo. 69% fill from ZipRecruiter itself; the remainder is lifted from
the employer's own domain where one is known.

job_is_remote.description:
Whether the job can be done remotely. A real tri-state here: ZipRecruiter states a
workplace type on 100% of postings, so `false` is a supported answer.
Fully remote and remote-optional map to `true`; hybrid and in-person map to `false`.

job_longitude.description: Always `null`, for the same reason as `job_latitude`.

job_posted_at.description:
Relative publication age, for example `4 days ago` or `1 month ago`. Derived from
ZipRecruiter's own posted-at stamp. Its JSON-LD `datePosted` is a reindex stamp and
disagrees with reality on 58% of postings.

job_publisher.description: Always `ZipRecruiter`. Constant by construction on this source.

job_apply_link.description:
The canonical ZipRecruiter posting URL, with tracking parameters stripped. 100% fill,
stable, and a page a human can apply from.

Qualifications: At least 3 years of experience programming with Python, Go, Scala, or Java
Responsibilities: Design, develop, test, deploy, and support AI software components.

job_highlights.description:
Description bullets grouped by section, keyed `Qualifications`, `Responsibilities` and
`Benefits`. Recovered from the posting's own headed lists, plus ZipRecruiter's extracted
key responsibilities where it provides them. Detail surface only, 72% fill; `{}` when
nothing was recovered, so it is always safe to enumerate. Only headings that map to one
of the three sections are kept.

job_max_salary.description: Upper bound of the stated range, in the `job_salary_period` unit. 69% fill.

job_min_salary.description: Lower bound of the stated range, in the `job_salary_period` unit. 69% fill.

At Capital One, we are creating responsible and reliable AI systems, changing banking for good.
job_description.description:
The full posting text, HTML stripped to plain text with paragraph breaks preserved.
**Detail surface only, and this is the field callers most often expect for free:** it
is `null` on a `/search` response unless `include_details=true`, because a ZipRecruiter
search card carries only a roughly 200-character teaser, published separately as
`ziprecruiter_short_description`. 100% fill on the detail surface.

job_google_link.description:
Always `null`. This link is a Google for Jobs construction built around a Google docid,
which ZipRecruiter does not issue.

employer_reviews.description:
Employer ratings published by Breakroom. Detail surface only, 14% fill; `null` when
ZipRecruiter shows no rating. Note the scale is 1 to 10, carried on the row as
`max_score`.

employer_website.description:
The employer's own website, from ZipRecruiter's company widget. Detail surface only,
54% fill.

job_onet_job_zone.description:
Always `null`. The O*NET job zone is a Google enrichment; ZipRecruiter states the SOC
code only.

job_salary_period.description: The period the salary figures are expressed in. 69% fill.

job_salary_string.description: ZipRecruiter's own salary text, verbatim, exactly as shown on the page. 69% fill.

job_apply_is_direct.description:
Always `false`. A ZipApply job is applied to on ZipRecruiter, and an external job goes
through a redirect whose destination is an ad network relay more often than an employer
ATS. See `ziprecruiter_apply_type` for the apply signal.

job_employment_type.description:
The first entry of `job_employment_types`, for JSearch compatibility. `null` when
ZipRecruiter states no employment type. `INTERN` appears here as a reported value:
ZipRecruiter labels internships on the posting, while its search offers an
`employment_types` filter without one.

ziprecruiter_is_new.description:
ZipRecruiter's own "new" badge on a search card. Search surface only, and `null` when
the payload carries no badge.

job_benefits_strings.description:
ZipRecruiter's own benefit labels, split out of its single comma-joined display string.
Same 44% fill as `job_benefits`; `null` when none are stated.

job_employment_types.description:
Every employment type stated on the posting, in JSearch's documented order so two
identically tagged jobs always serialise the same way. An empty array when
ZipRecruiter states none. `INTERN` is a reported value here; ZipRecruiter's search
offers an `employment_types` filter without one.

ziprecruiter_share_url.description: ZipRecruiter's own short share link for the posting.

job_posted_at_timestamp.description: Unix timestamp in seconds of the publication date. 100% fill.

ziprecruiter_apply_host.description:
The hostname behind ZipRecruiter's external apply redirect, decoded. Provenance only:
it is frequently an ad network relay. Use `job_apply_link` to apply.

ziprecruiter_apply_type.description:
How applying works. `OPEN_APPLY_FLOW` is ZipApply, applied on ZipRecruiter itself;
`OPEN_EXTERNAL` leaves for a third-party destination. This is the apply signal to read.

ziprecruiter_company_hq.description:
The company's headquarters location from ZipRecruiter's company widget. Detail surface
only, 54% fill.

ziprecruiter_company_id.description:
ZipRecruiter's internal company identifier, an opaque base64 blob, stringified like
every other id in this response.

ziprecruiter_updated_at.description:
When ZipRecruiter last refreshed the listing, distinct from the publication date. Search
surface only: `null` on `/job-details`. Nanosecond precision, as ZipRecruiter publishes
it.

ziprecruiter_listing_key.description:
ZipRecruiter's internal listing key. Useful for diffing payloads, but NOT an identity:
the same job can carry different keys on different surfaces. Use `job_id` or `job_uid`.

ziprecruiter_location_id.description: ZipRecruiter's internal identifier for the location.

ziprecruiter_company_size.description:

search to this employer with `ziprecruiter_company_id`.

ziprecruiter_employer_faq.description:
ZipRecruiter's generated FAQ for the posting. Detail surface only. Despite the contract
name, most entries are about the ROLE; some are Breakroom survey findings about the

ziprecruiter_job_industry.description:

ziprecruiter_location_type.description:

Where ZipRecruiter's pay figure came from. Always published, even when the salary
fields are `null`, so a caller can see WHY a job has no salary: `SOURCE_MISSING` means
the employer stated no pay and ZipRecruiter modelled and then hid a figure, which this
API suppresses.

ziprecruiter_valid_through.description:
The date the posting expires, as ZipRecruiter states it in JSON-LD. Detail surface
only, capped at 73%.

ziprecruiter_ats_identifier.description:
The employer's own requisition reference, from the posting's JSON-LD identifier. Detail
surface only, and present on 40 of the 43 measured pages that carry JSON-LD at all.

ziprecruiter_location_county.description: County or equivalent administrative area for the job location.

caller omitted them and the caller's raw string when the caller supplied them.

job_id.description:
Stable, opaque id for this posting. Pass it straight back to `/job-details`. Encodes
ZipRecruiter's own seat id, so it survives re-fetches and is the same on every surface.

job_uid.description:
ZipRecruiter's own raw seat id, 16 hex characters. Stable across surfaces and
re-fetches, accepted directly by `/job-details`, and the right key for an enrichment
cache.

job_city.description: City. `null` on a state-level or remote-only listing.

job_state.description:
The full state or province NAME, matching JSearch. The two-letter code appears inside
`job_location`.

job_title.description: The job title as ZipRecruiter publishes it. 100% fill.

job_salary.description:
The headline salary figure: the midpoint when the posting states a range, the single
bound otherwise, in the period given by `job_salary_period`. 69% fill. Populated only
when ZipRecruiter itself displays the pay.

job_country.description: Uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. `US` or `CA` on this source.

job_benefits.description:
Normalised benefit tags ZipRecruiter states on the posting. 44% fill; `null` when none
are stated.

job_latitude.description:
Always `null`. ZipRecruiter publishes coordinates on neither the card, the detail
payload nor the JSON-LD.

job_location.description: The location as ZipRecruiter displays it on the posting. 100% fill.

job_onet_soc.description:
The O*NET-SOC occupation code ZipRecruiter states, with the human title removed.
Detail surface only, and capped at 73% because it comes from JSON-LD, which
ZipRecruiter ships on 73% of detail pages.

apply_options.description:
Ways to apply. ZipRecruiter exposes exactly one, its own posting page, so this is a
one-entry array, or empty on the rare job with no resolvable URL.

employer_logo.description:
The employer's logo. 69% fill from ZipRecruiter itself; the remainder is lifted from
the employer's own domain where one is known.

job_is_remote.description:
Whether the job can be done remotely. A real tri-state here: ZipRecruiter states a
workplace type on 100% of postings, so `false` is a supported answer.
Fully remote and remote-optional map to `true`; hybrid and in-person map to `false`.

job_longitude.description: Always `null`, for the same reason as `job_latitude`.

job_posted_at.description:
Relative publication age, for example `4 days ago` or `1 month ago`. Derived from
ZipRecruiter's own posted-at stamp. Its JSON-LD `datePosted` is a reindex stamp and
disagrees with reality on 58% of postings.

job_publisher.description: Always `ZipRecruiter`. Constant by construction on this source.

job_apply_link.description:
The canonical ZipRecruiter posting URL, with tracking parameters stripped. 100% fill,
stable, and a page a human can apply from.

Qualifications: At least 3 years of experience programming with Python, Go, Scala, or Java
Responsibilities: Design, develop, test, deploy, and support AI software components.

job_highlights.description:
Description bullets grouped by section, keyed `Qualifications`, `Responsibilities` and
`Benefits`. Recovered from the posting's own headed lists, plus ZipRecruiter's extracted
key responsibilities where it provides them. Detail surface only, 72% fill; `{}` when
nothing was recovered, so it is always safe to enumerate. Only headings that map to one
of the three sections are kept.

job_max_salary.description: Upper bound of the stated range, in the `job_salary_period` unit. 69% fill.

job_min_salary.description: Lower bound of the stated range, in the `job_salary_period` unit. 69% fill.

job_description.example:
Senior AI Engineer (AI Foundations)

Overview:

At Capital One, we are creating responsible and reliable AI systems, changing banking for good.
job_description.description:
The full posting text, HTML stripped to plain text with paragraph breaks preserved.
**Detail surface only, and this is the field callers most often expect for free:** it
is `null` on a `/search` response unless `include_details=true`, because a ZipRecruiter
search card carries only a roughly 200-character teaser, published separately as
`ziprecruiter_short_description`. 100% fill on the detail surface.

job_google_link.description:
Always `null`. This link is a Google for Jobs construction built around a Google docid,
which ZipRecruiter does not issue.

employer_reviews.description:
Employer ratings published by Breakroom. Detail surface only, 14% fill; `null` when
ZipRecruiter shows no rating. Note the scale is 1 to 10, carried on the row as
`max_score`.

employer_website.description:
The employer's own website, from ZipRecruiter's company widget. Detail surface only,
54% fill.

job_onet_job_zone.description:
Always `null`. The O*NET job zone is a Google enrichment; ZipRecruiter states the SOC
code only.

job_salary_period.description: The period the salary figures are expressed in. 69% fill.

job_salary_string.description: ZipRecruiter's own salary text, verbatim, exactly as shown on the page. 69% fill.

job_apply_is_direct.description:
Always `false`. A ZipApply job is applied to on ZipRecruiter, and an external job goes
through a redirect whose destination is an ad network relay more often than an employer
ATS. See `ziprecruiter_apply_type` for the apply signal.

job_employment_type.description:
The first entry of `job_employment_types`, for JSearch compatibility. `null` when
ZipRecruiter states no employment type. `INTERN` appears here as a reported value:
ZipRecruiter labels internships on the posting, while its search offers an
`employment_types` filter without one.

ziprecruiter_is_new.description:
ZipRecruiter's own "new" badge on a search card. Search surface only, and `null` when
the payload carries no badge.

job_benefits_strings.description:
ZipRecruiter's own benefit labels, split out of its single comma-joined display string.
Same 44% fill as `job_benefits`; `null` when none are stated.

job_employment_types.description:
Every employment type stated on the posting, in JSearch's documented order so two
identically tagged jobs always serialise the same way. An empty array when
ZipRecruiter states none. `INTERN` is a reported value here; ZipRecruiter's search
offers an `employment_types` filter without one.

ziprecruiter_share_url.description: ZipRecruiter's own short share link for the posting.

job_posted_at_timestamp.description: Unix timestamp in seconds of the publication date. 100% fill.

ziprecruiter_apply_host.description:
The hostname behind ZipRecruiter's external apply redirect, decoded. Provenance only:
it is frequently an ad network relay. Use `job_apply_link` to apply.

ziprecruiter_apply_type.description:
How applying works. `OPEN_APPLY_FLOW` is ZipApply, applied on ZipRecruiter itself;
`OPEN_EXTERNAL` leaves for a third-party destination. This is the apply signal to read.

ziprecruiter_company_hq.description:
The company's headquarters location from ZipRecruiter's company widget. Detail surface
only, 54% fill.

ziprecruiter_company_id.description:
ZipRecruiter's internal company identifier, an opaque base64 blob, stringified like
every other id in this response.

ziprecruiter_updated_at.description:
When ZipRecruiter last refreshed the listing, distinct from the publication date. Search
surface only: `null` on `/job-details`. Nanosecond precision, as ZipRecruiter publishes
it.

ziprecruiter_listing_key.description:
ZipRecruiter's internal listing key. Useful for diffing payloads, but NOT an identity:
the same job can carry different keys on different surfaces. Use `job_id` or `job_uid`.

ziprecruiter_location_id.description: ZipRecruiter's internal identifier for the location.

ziprecruiter_company_size.description:
Employee headcount band from ZipRecruiter's company widget, for example
`1001 - 5000 Employees`. Detail surface only, 54% fill.

ziprecruiter_company_slug.description:
ZipRecruiter's canonical display name for the company. A display label only: scope a
search to this employer with `ziprecruiter_company_id`.

ziprecruiter_employer_faq.description:
ZipRecruiter's generated FAQ for the posting. Detail surface only. Despite the contract
name, most entries are about the ROLE; some are Breakroom survey findings about the
employer.

ziprecruiter_job_industry.description:
The industry ZipRecruiter assigns to this JOB. From JSON-LD, so detail surface only and
capped at 73%.

ziprecruiter_location_type.description:
ZipRecruiter's own workplace-type enum, passed through verbatim. 100% fill, and the
source `job_is_remote` is derived from.

ziprecruiter_salary_source.description:
Where ZipRecruiter's pay figure came from. Always published, even when the salary
fields are `null`, so a caller can see WHY a job has no salary: `SOURCE_MISSING` means
the employer stated no pay and ZipRecruiter modelled and then hid a figure, which this
API suppresses.

ziprecruiter_valid_through.description:
The date the posting expires, as ZipRecruiter states it in JSON-LD. Detail surface
only, capped at 73%.

ziprecruiter_ats_identifier.description:
The employer's own requisition reference, from the posting's JSON-LD identifier. Detail
surface only, and present on 40 of the 43 measured pages that carry JSON-LD at all.

ziprecruiter_location_county.description: County or equivalent administrative area for the job location.

ziprecruiter_description_html.example:
Senior AI Engineer (AI Foundations)

Overview:

At Capital One, we are creating responsible ...
ziprecruiter_description_html.description:
The job description with ZipRecruiter's original HTML markup preserved, for callers who
want the formatting. Detail surface only, 100% fill there.

ziprecruiter_canonical_job_url.description:
The canonical ZipRecruiter posting URL. Identical to `job_apply_link`, exposed under
its own name so the ZipRecruiter extras stand on their own.

ziprecruiter_short_description.example: Senior AI Engineer (AI Foundations) Overview: At Capital One, we are creating responsible and reliable AI systems, changing banking for good.
ziprecruiter_short_description.description:
The roughly 200-character teaser a ZipRecruiter search card carries. Card surface
only: always `null` on `/job-details`, where the full `job_description` is present
instead. Passed through verbatim, so unlike `job_description` it can carry
ZipRecruiter's own `<b>` search-highlight markup and undecoded HTML entities; strip or
decode it before display.

ziprecruiter_company_industries.description:
Industries ZipRecruiter assigns to the COMPANY, distinct from the job's own industry.
Detail surface only; `null` when the widget lists none.

ziprecruiter_salary_is_estimated.description:
Whether ZipRecruiter labels the displayed pay as an estimate. `null` when there is no
displayed pay to label.

ziprecruiter_key_responsibilities.description:
ZipRecruiter's machine-extracted responsibility summaries, rewritten from the posting.
Detail surface only, present on roughly a third of detail pages; also merged into
`job_highlights.Responsibilities`.

ziprecruiter_location_postal_code.description: Postal or ZIP code, as a string so leading zeros survive.

sds_L_Fsr74jXxRwFrRFUiukT_24e03882eaa99c.description:
A ZipRecruiter job posting. A superset of the 35-key JSearch `/search` contract, whose keys
come first in contract order, followed by 25 `ziprecruiter_*` extras, for 60 keys in total.
Every key is always present, `null` / `[]` / `{}` where ZipRecruiter has no value, so a
consumer gets the same set of keys on every job. The `fields` projection narrows it,
returning exactly the keys asked for plus `job_id` and `job_title`.

Fields marked "detail surface only" are `null` on a `/search` response unless
`include_details=true`, and are filled on `/job-details`.

is_direct.description: Always `false`. The destination is ZipRecruiter itself or an ad network relay.

publisher.description: Always `ZipRecruiter`; every row on this surface is a ZipRecruiter listing.

apply_link.description: The canonical ZipRecruiter posting URL, identical to `job_apply_link`.

sds_L_Fsr74jXxRwFrRFUiukT_24e03882eaa99c.description:
One way to apply to this job. ZipRecruiter exposes exactly one, its own posting page, so
this array has either one entry or none.

score.description: The rating, on the `max_score` scale, rounded to 2 decimals.

max_score.description: The top of the scale. `10` for Breakroom.

num_stars.description: `score` rounded to the nearest whole number, on the same scale as `max_score`.

publisher.description: Who published the rating. `Breakroom` on every sample measured.

review_count.description: How many responses the rating is based on.

reviews_link.description: The Breakroom company page the rating comes from.

employer_name.description: The employer the rating is about, as the rating source names it.

sds_L_Fsr74jXxRwFrRFUiukT_24e03882eaa99c.description:
One employer rating, published by Breakroom. Note the scale: `max_score` is 10, and the
score is carried on that scale unchanged.

answer.example: Key technical skills include expertise in programming languages such as Java, Python, or C++.
answer.description: The answer, verbatim. May contain inline HTML where ZipRecruiter published it.

question.example: What skills or qualities help someone succeed as a Senior Software Engineer?

sds_L_Fsr74jXxRwFrRFUiukT_24e03882eaa99c.description:
One generated FAQ entry. ZipRecruiter writes these about the ROLE, so most answers
describe the occupation; a few are Breakroom survey findings about the employer.

code.description: HTTP status code, repeated in the body.

message.description: Human-readable explanation, naming the parameter and the allowed values.

request_id.description: Unique id for this request, useful when contacting support.

sds_L_Fsr74jXxRwFrRFUiukT_24e03882eaa99c.description:
The requested resource does not exist. On `/search` this is an unrecognised `company_id`,
and on `/estimated-salary` a job title, or a title and state pair, outside ZipRecruiter's
salary pages.
Quota exhausted or rate limit hit.

ZipRecruiter was temporarily unreachable after the full proxy ladder was exhausted. A 503
means the page could not be read, where an empty result set means the search ran and
matched nothing. Safe to retry.
